---
title: "Gaussianization"
---

Turn messy, dependent data into a **standard Gaussian** — where every coordinate
is independent and everything is easy — using a map that is **invertible**.  That
single requirement is what makes Gaussianization the hinge of the whole course:
run the map *forward* to measure and remove dependence, run it *backward* to
generate it.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## The Spine — One Invertible Map, Both Directions

$$
\underbrace{z = T(x)}_{\text{forward: simplify}}
\qquad\qquad
\underbrace{x = T^{-1}(z)}_{\text{backward: generate}}
$$

Forward, $T$ Gaussianizes — and the distortion it needs is *exactly* the
dependence in the data.  Backward, you draw an easy Gaussian sample and invert it
to recover the real, dependent world.  Measuring (Ch. 1), removing (Ch. 4), and
[propagating](../uncertainty/index.qmd) (Ch. 3) are three uses of this one map.
:::

## Why It Sits Here

- **Change of variables** — $p_X(x) = p_Z(T(x))\,\lvert\det J_T\rvert$ — is the
  same Jacobian rule that powers [Uncertainty](../uncertainty/index.qmd).
- **MI estimation** — Gaussianizing makes mutual information and total
  correlation tractable in high dimensions, the density road from
  [Chapter 1](../dependence/index.qmd).
- **Code:** [rbig](https://github.com/jejjohnson/rbig) (rotation-based iterative
  Gaussianization) and [gauss_flows](https://github.com/jejjohnson/gauss_flows)
  (normalizing flows).  This chapter's figures call the real `rbig` package
  (`from rbig import AnnealedRBIG`) — it is NumPy/scikit-learn based, so it
  renders without the heavy JAX/Keras libraries.

## The Ladder

| Rung | Idea | Tool |
|------|------|------|
| 1 | Change of variables & the Jacobian | the density-transformation rule |
| 2 | Marginal Gaussianize + rotate, iterated | **RBIG** |
| 3 | Read dependence as information removed | MI / total correlation via RBIG |
| 4 | Learn the map directly | normalizing **flows** |

## Pages in This Chapter

1. **[Change of variables](01-change-of-variables.qmd)** — how a density
   transforms under an invertible map, and the 1-D rank → Gaussian trick.
2. **[RBIG](02-rbig.qmd)** — marginal Gaussianization plus rotation, iterated to
   a spherical Gaussian; and run backward to sample.
3. **[Mutual information via Gaussianization](03-mutual-information.qmd)** — the
   dependence removed *is* the information shared; total correlation in nats.
4. **[Normalizing flows](04-flows.qmd)** — learned, flexible Gaussianization when
   RBIG's fixed structure is not enough.

The hands-on [labs](labs/index.qmd) build the 1-D transform, the full RBIG loop,
an MI estimator, and a generator on real returns.
